title: Five House Dressings
subtitle: Recipe Formulation Sheet

source.author: Julee Rosso and Sheila Lukins
source.note: The All-Purpose Vinaigrette formula is adapted from The Silver Palate. The remaining four dressings are house formulations.

summary: Five emulsions covering most of what a salad needs. The All-Purpose is the workhorse — deliberately flexible, since it tolerates any vinegar and any soft herb on hand. Lemon-Dijon is the same idea with brightness and less flavor of its own. Sesame-Soy is built to cut richness, which is why it lands best on slaws. The Caesar skips the raw egg in favor of mayonnaise, which is already emulsified oil and egg. The Creamy Herby Green is the one worth breaking out a blender for.
scalingPrinciple: Each formulation locks its own oil (or, for the creamy dressings, its primary lipid or dairy base) at 100.0% so the oil-to-acid ratio — the only number that really governs a vinaigrette — reads directly off each matrix. The batch scaler drives all five proportionally from the All-Purpose baseline.

formulations.title: 1. All-Purpose Vinaigrette
formulations.intro: The default. Reduce oil to 1/3 cup (~72 g, 66.7%) if you like your dressing more aggressive. Vegan.

rows.name: Neutral or Olive Oil
rows.role: Lipid phase; streamed in last to build the emulsion.

rows.name: Vinegar (red, white, white balsamic, or sherry)
rows.role: Primary acid. Any vinegar works — this is the flexible axis.

rows.name: Dijon Mustard
rows.role: Emulsifier; the lecithin that holds oil and acid together.

rows.name: Fresh Lemon Juice
rows.role: Secondary acid; adds a brighter top note than vinegar alone.

rows.name: Fresh Chopped Herbs (parsley, chives, tarragon, dill, basil)
rows.role: Whatever is on hand — the second flexible axis.

formulations.title: 2. Lemon-Dijon
formulations.intro: Interchangeable with the All-Purpose, but reach for it when you want brightness without adding much flavor of its own. Vegan if you swap sugar for the honey.

rows.name: Fresh Lemon Juice
rows.role: Sole acid; the point of the dressing.

formulations.title: 3. Sesame-Soy Dressing
formulations.intro: Best on slaws, where the job is cutting richness. Add chives, cilantro, or dill freely. Substitute tamari for the soy sauce to make it gluten-free. Vegan.

rows.name: Grapeseed or Other Neutral Oil
rows.role: Lipid phase; neutral so the sesame reads clearly.

rows.name: Rice Wine Vinegar
rows.role: Primary acid; unusually high ratio, which is what makes this one bright.

rows.name: Toasted Sesame Oil
rows.role: Aromatic finishing oil — not a structural fat.

formulations.title: 4. Classic Caesar
formulations.intro: Drizzle on any salad, not just a Caesar. Mayonnaise replaces the traditional raw egg. For a stronger version, increase garlic to two cloves and anchovies to three fillets.

rows.name: Mayonnaise
rows.role: Pre-made emulsion standing in for raw egg yolk.

rows.name: Red Wine Vinegar
rows.role: Second acid; sharper than lemon alone.

formulations.title: 5. Creamy Herby Green Dressing
formulations.intro: Worth the blender. Best when herbs are abundant. Try it over roasted beets or broccoli, or alongside grilled fish. Vegan if you replace the yogurt with a slightly smaller quantity of cashew cream (about 1/3 cup).

rows.name: Plain Yogurt
rows.role: Creamy base; the structural phase in place of a pure oil emulsion.

rows.name: Avocado
rows.role: Body and richness; carries the green color.

rows.name: Scallions (light green and white parts), chopped
Water
rows.role: Consistency control; add 1 tbsp at a time until pourable.

matrixFootnote: *These formulations are given entirely in volumetric kitchen units in the source. All gram values are standard culinary conversions and are marked accordingly; none are source-stated weights. Percentages are calculated within each dressing against its own lipid or dairy base, not across formulations.

execution.name: Shaken Vinaigrettes (1, 2, 3)
execution.text: In a small jar or measuring cup, shake or whisk together everything except the oil until the salt and any sugar have fully dissolved. Then shake or whisk the oil into the jar in a steady stream until emulsified. Adding the oil last and gradually is what separates a stable dressing from one that splits on the plate.

execution.name: Blended Caesar (4)
execution.text: Purée the garlic, anchovy, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, olive oil, mayonnaise, Parmesan, salt, and pepper until smooth.

execution.name: Blended Green (5)
execution.text: Add the yogurt, parsley, chives, white wine vinegar, avocado, olive oil, scallions, honey, salt, pepper, and about 2 tbsp of water to a blender. Process until creamy but not too thick, and pourable — keeping in mind you may have to add more water, one tablespoon at a time.

directive: For the three shaken vinaigrettes, dissolve the salt in the acid phase before any oil goes in. Salt will not dissolve into an established emulsion, and undissolved crystals read as harsh grit on the greens.
